title: Space Force weapons may signal shift in US defense strategy: Ross Coulthart
byline: Alicia Sitz, Hena Doba, and Ross Coulthart
excerpt: Coulthart recalled that in May 2024, military officials told NewsNation’s Brian Entin the U.S. did not have weapons in orbit.
content:
(NewsNation) — Foreign adversaries are criticizing the U.S. after Air Force officials announced on Sept. 14 that Space Force had launched defensive weapons into space.

Investigative journalist Ross Coulthart says it may mark a change in the country’s defense strategy. He also says many questions remain about what has actually been deployed.

What could Space Force’s new weapons do?

Coulthart told NewsNation’s Hena Doba on Sunday that the U.S. may be reacting to possible threats in space from Russia and China. He said the new capabilities might involve technology that can jam communications or interfere with other countries’ satellites.

“One of the speculations I’m hearing from my sources is that what they’re talking about is a capacity to jam frequencies, or perhaps to dazzle rival adversary satellites,” Coulthart said.

He recalled that when NewsNation’s Brian Entin reported on Space Force operations in May 2024, military officials said the U.S. did not have weapons in orbit at the time.

“If this has happened, it’s happened very, very recently,” he said.

The discussion also covered unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAPs, and whether the government might release more information about them.

Was Trump told about a secret UAP program?

The Pentagon has said it has found no evidence that the U.S. government or private companies have copied, or tried to copy, technology from outside Earth. The Reality Check host said he believes the government has more information about UAPs than it has shared with the public.

Citing his own reporting and unnamed sources, Coulthart said efforts have been made to attract and shoot down UAPs at White Sands Missile Range.

He also said his sources claim that President Donald Trump was told about a secret UAP program and approved an investigation into whether private aerospace companies have technology that is not human-made.

“I’m told that President Trump has become aware of the legacy program,” Coulthart said, adding that the investigation is intended to determine “who the private aerospace companies are that are controlling this alleged non-human technology.”

There was no evidence shown during the interview to confirm the existence of the program or the investigation into non-human technology.

Coulthart said he thinks the White House is now weighing whether to release more information about UAPs to the public.

“The White House is wrestling with a decision about whether to disclose,” he said.

What is ‘catastrophic disclosure’?

Coulthart also discussed what he called ‘catastrophic disclosure,’ which he described as information coming out in an uncontrolled way that governments would rather keep secret.

Referring to comments from UAP whistleblower David Grusch, he said that new developments in artificial intelligence could make it harder to keep secrets. He also said that people who know about what he described as a secret UAP programs are becoming more frustrated with the lack of openness.

“There are people inside the legacy program who, frankly, have had enough of the secrecy,” Coulthart said. “They think the American public have a right to know.”
